## Triage: first grade — `bug` · `priority:p2` · `domain:server` · `area:devpath` · `pm:queue` · triage seat · `session_01AavokzJ5DndAwitDXvKy4U` · 2026-10-25T15:59Z

⛔ Not a claim, ⛔ not a dispatch.

- **p2:** build time and publish time disagree on what a package may reference. The fix: the validate, lint and build reference ladder reads the `manifest.dependencies` closure the publish gate already uses. No spec key changes.

  "issue": 25805,
  "status": "needs_decision",
  "branch": "claude/project-thread-05lflq",

  "premise_still_valid": true,
  "summary": "The defect reproduces, but the order's mechanism hypothesis is falsified: build time cannot reach the publish gate's closure without a running kernel or the network, so per the order I stopped before any edit. The gate's closure is computed by the private `resolveWritePackageScope` in packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol.ts: it walks `engine.registry.getPackage(id).manifest.dependencies` transitively in a LIVE kernel, and the object names come from registry rows stamped `_packageId` (`narrowObjectsToPackageClosure`, packages/lint/src/runtime-gate.ts). A `manifest.dependencies` key is a package id resolved by the catalog (`os package install` fetches it from the runtime's configured catalog, OS_CLOUD_URL) or by an installed runtime; nothing maps such an id to a file the CLI could open. No node_modules route (HotCRM is `private: true`, published only to the marketplace via scripts/publish-marketplace.mjs) and no lockfile artifact exists (zero hits for a lockfile shape in packages/spec/src). packages/cli/src/utils/picklist-references.ts already measured and wrote down this same limit for picklists. One more measured fact changes the weighing: on the runtime side, `validateObjectReferences` crosses only `runtimeTypes: ['flow', 'dataset']` (packages/lint/src/reference-integrity-suite.ts), so a field `reference` written through an object write is not judged by the publish gate at all. For lookup targets the build is the ONLY door, and the card's 'publish gate already resolves that closure' holds for flow trigger objects, dataset base objects and list-view bindings, not for `Field.lookup`. No edit, no PR; the decision is below.",
  "tests": "Red first, measured on published @objectstack/cli 18.1.0 (npm), with a scratch fixture outside every repo: stack `app.acme.clm`, `manifest.dependencies: { 'app.objectstack.hotcrm': '^6.0.0' }`, object `clm_contract` with `Field.lookup('crm_contract')` and `sharingModel: 'private'`, and a `record-after-update` flow on `crm_contract`. `os validate` exit 1, one issue: object-reference-unknown at objects[0].fields.crm_contract.reference. `os build` exit 1, same single error plus warning flow-trigger-unknown-object at flows[0].nodes[0].config.objectName. `os lint` exit 1, object-reference-unknown error, flow-trigger-unknown-object warning. origin/main 05f7758f carries the same ladder (`artifactProvidedObjectNames`, read in source). No repo test written: nothing was changed, so the red test lands with whichever option is ruled.",
  "gates": "NOT MEASURED: no diff, so there is no change set to derive gates from and nothing to run.",
  "dogfood_battery": "n/a: no PR",
  "mcp_calls": "0",
  "api_writes": "1: POST /repos/objectstack-ai/objectstack/issues/25805/comments (this report, via scripts/pm/post-stamped.mjs)",
  "open_questions": [
    {
      "status": "needs_decision",
      "question": "Build time cannot read the objects of a package named in `manifest.dependencies` that the artifact does not carry, since that needs the catalog or a running kernel. What should `os validate` / `os lint` / `os build` do with a lookup target or trigger object that such a package might provide?",
      "options": [
        "A. Advisory arm, the picklist precedent: when the declaring package names a dependency outside the artifact, an unresolved unprefixed name is downgraded from error to a non-gating notice that names the dependencies (the shape `picklist-reference-unverified` uses). Work: small, in lint and the CLI. Business need: unblocks hotclm today. Long term: this is consumer-side leniency, and it is permanent, because the closure stays unreadable. AI mistakes: weakest option. A typo like `crm_contrat` in any stack with one external dependency becomes a notice, and nothing later refuses it: the publish gate does not judge field `reference` on object writes. That is #16611's silent class returning for every app that has a dependency. Startup focus: smallest surface, but it breaks ruling 2 in substance, since a name nobody provides no longer errors.",
        "B. An explicit local input of dependency artifacts: the CLI takes compiled dependency artifacts (`dist/objectstack.json`) from a path the project names, through a CLI flag or the project's CLI config, never a spec key. It reads their package bodies with the existing artifact reader (`resolveArtifactPackageEntries` in @objectstack/core) and resolves names against the transitive `dependencies` closure. That walk is extracted ONCE out of `resolveWritePackageScope` into a shared function that both the protocol and the CLI call, so there is no second resolver. A declared dependency with no supplied artifact keeps today's error, and the hint adds 'supply its artifact'. Work: medium, covering core (extract the walk), lint (one extra resolvable set) and the CLI (input and wiring). Business need: serves hotclm exactly, but hotclm's CI has to get HotCRM's artifact onto disk (a release asset, a submodule or a build step), because HotCRM is not on npm. Long term: exact and contract-first. It is the same closure the gate uses, fed with real artifacts and no guess. AI mistakes: strongest option. Every unresolved name still errors, and a supplied artifact cannot make up a name. Startup focus: one new CLI input with a named external user (hotclm#107) and no new gate.",
        "C. Catalog fetch at build: the CLI resolves each dependency id at its declared range from the marketplace catalog, the same source `os package install` uses, and caches the snapshot. Work: large, covering a catalog client in the CLI, range resolution, caching, and an offline policy. Business need: also serves hotclm, with no artifact plumbing in its CI. Long term: exact, but every build depends on the network, and the version resolved at build can differ from the one resolved at install. AI mistakes: as strict as B when the fetch works. The offline arm is the trap: if it fails open it is option A, and if it fails closed it blocks offline builds. Startup focus: the largest surface for one consumer.",
        "D. Keep the error and resolve nothing new. Work: zero. Business need: hotclm stays blocked. Its own maintainer refused both workarounds, bundling HotCRM into its artifact and turning the link into a text id. Long term: build and publish keep disagreeing for flows. AI mistakes: strict. Startup focus: best on scope, but it fails a measured, named need."
      ],
      "recommendation": "B. It is the only option that keeps ruling 2 (an unresolvable name stays an error) while serving the named real consumer, hotclm#107, offline. It reuses the gate's closure walk as one extracted function instead of writing a second one, and it adds no spec key and no gate. A is cheaper, but it re-opens #16611's silent typo class for every app with a dependency: for `Field.lookup` the build is the only door that judges the name. C buys hotclm less CI plumbing at the cost of network-coupled builds, and it can follow B later as another source of the same artifacts. If B is ruled, the dispatch needs one more line: the flag or config spelling, which is a CLI surface to name, not a spec key."
    }
  ],
  "out_of_scope_findings": [
    "carrier: none. Noted, not filed: `object-reference-unknown` on a field `reference` does not cross the runtime publish gate for object writes (validateObjectReferences runtimeTypes = flow, dataset), so a Studio or REST `/meta` object save with a dangling lookup target is not refused. This is read from source, not exercised through a door, so no reach was measured and the case does not qualify for filing."
  ]
